findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The observer feature, spec, dimensions, recovery plan and proof map are consistent, and I found no blocking errors. The numbers check out against each other: 12 scenario blocks compile to 17 cases (R1 4, R2 6, R3 2, R4 4, R5 1). The proof map lists 11 test files, which matches the inventory, and the totals of 37 cases and 33 deferrals agree with proof-inventory.json. Every Rule clause that has no acceptance scenario is assigned to a named lower-level matrix in dimensions.md. That covers scope changes before execution, dirty staged, unstaged or untracked inputs, wrong-purpose and unauthenticated records, duplicate or ambiguous results, refused-path history preservation, and paired controls for meaning changes versus bookkeeping-only changes. Authority boundaries are explicit and match the ticket's scope and out-of-scope lists: the observer grants no RED, certification or closing authority, and the 33 deferrals stay uncredited. The remaining concerns are design or feasibility risks for implementation planning, not omissions that would let a false success pass.

The demo scenario assumes all 37 delivery cases can be honestly mapped to named assertions. proof-map.md's certification gap says otherwise for some cases. Fallback order must cover both declaration orders and both success and failure branches, but one parameterized title maps it. Route admission must separate the wrong-identity outcome from stale digests, and the degraded-labeling test is only supporting evidence. If a case can't be supported, R2 correctly refuses, but then the @demo scenario can't pass without new tests. Implementation planning should check mapping feasibility early and record which outcome is acceptable: a refusal that names the unsupported case, or separately scoped new proof.

R4 and the shipped-profile matrix protect required assertion names: removing or renaming one can't shrink the required set. A committed edit that empties a test body but keeps its title still makes the candidate stale, but the next observation of that new candidate would succeed. The spec deliberately puts semantic adequacy in later certification. Planning should state that the observation keeps each test-source digest in a form a certifier can compare with the reviewed baseline (for example, the inventory's file hashes). Otherwise the phrase 'trustworthy current proof' could be read as covering more than assertion execution.

In the context file keep-bounded-planning-reviews-trustworthy.bdd-proof.json, three blocks use a different shape: 'A malformed plan record…', 'Refused selectors…' and 'A failed independent attempt…' are flat [file, title] pairs, while the other blocks are arrays of pairs. The observer's shipped contract must not take its required set from this project-editable file anyway (R1). Still, any tool that derives the reviewed contract from it must normalize both shapes, or it may silently drop or misread required assertions.

The mid-run candidate scenario says the candidate 'advances to another commit' while execution runs. The plan runs the lane in an isolated checkout, so a commit advancing in the original checkout may never touch the running inputs. dimensions.md requires strict refusal anyway, and also needs an in-place change to lockfile, config or support files while the run is paused. Planning should say which checkout's HEAD and input digests are re-checked after execution, so the check actually distinguishes stable from changed candidates and can't pass vacuously because of isolation.

The retry scenario's Given clause doesn't state that the fixed lane now passes on the same candidate, yet its Then clause expects a successful observation. The intent (a transient interruption) is clear, but adding that precondition would make the scenario fully specified.

The altered-report recovery action asks for 'a new observation of the unchanged committed candidate'. If the candidate has also changed since then, verification should probably report the more specific currency problem first. That ordering can be left to the observer-recovery-messages matrix.
